Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "hello Mara, i'm asking for a correction to the Sunday, March 14, issue of the Pine Ledger, page 6, in the article called “A Pier Returns to Work.” The caption under the archival photograph says that the woman at the left is former councilor Lena Ortiz. That is wrong: the woman is Ruth Bell, who was a volunteer at the East Quay ferry terminal reopening. The caption also leaves out the terminal manager, Simon Dale, who is beside her. I am writing for the East Quay Local History Association, but Ruth checked the photograph herself before I sent this, and she says her name should be corrected.

The photograph was taken on October 2, 1986, during the reopening event. The city archive lists it as image 86-117, and its catalog description names “Ruth Bell, left, and terminal manager Simon Dale.” Our association has the event program, which also lists Ruth as a schedule volunteer and Dale as terminal manager. I compared the printed image with the archive scan this morning; the same railing, banner, and people are visible in both. The paper's caption does not say where the image came from, so readers may not know there is a catalog record to check.

Ruth told me by phone on Monday at 9:10 a.m., “I was handing out the first-day schedules; Lena wasn't on the council yet.” The dates support what she said: Ortiz joined the council in 1989, three years after the reopening. I am not asking you to change the article's account of the terminal project or its opening date. The problem is only the identification in the photograph caption, and the correct names and roles are supported by the city archive and the event program.

Please check the page deadline before making the print change. If the March 14 edition has not been locked by 4:30 p.m. today, please replace the caption on page 6 with the wording in section 1 below. If the edition has already been locked, please do not change the printed pages; instead, put the correction online before noon tomorrow and include it in the next print edition, using section 2. In either case, please also correct the caption attached to the online article, since it currently repeats the same identification. The online page has a separate image caption field, so changing the article text alone would not fix it.

1. If the page is still open, use this replacement caption: “Ruth Bell, left, and East Quay terminal manager Simon Dale at the ferry terminal reopening on October 2, 1986. (City archive, image 86-117.)” Please keep the image credit in parentheses. It identifies the source and distinguishes this photograph from the two other East Quay reopening images in the archive catalog. The sentence in the article about the terminal's first passenger service can stay as written; it is not part of the error I am reporting.

2. If the page is locked, use this correction text online and in the next print edition: “A caption on page 6 of the March 14 Pine Ledger incorrectly identified Ruth Bell as former councilor Lena Ortiz. Bell was a volunteer at the East Quay ferry terminal reopening on October 2, 1986. The photograph also shows terminal manager Simon Dale. The city archive identifies the image as 86-117.” Please use the full correction rather than only changing the online photo caption in this branch, because readers who saw the printed issue need to be told what was incorrect. The correction should be labeled as a correction, not as a new article.

The association can provide a scan of the event program and a link to the archive catalog if your staff needs them. The catalog entry is searchable by the number 86-117, and the program's volunteer list is on its second page. Ruth has said she is willing to confirm her identification again, but please contact her through the association rather than publishing her phone number. Her permission to confirm the photograph is not permission to print personal contact details.

One timing point may affect the online update: if the web article is scheduled for its regular caption review after the print deadline, please do not wait for that review before correcting the image caption. The correction text can be added to the article page when it is posted, but the image field should also be changed as soon as the editor confirms which print branch applies. If staff cannot confirm the archive record before the relevant deadline, please hold the replacement caption until it is checked rather than substituting another name. The catalog description and event program are available for that check.

For the record, the association first noticed the caption when a member brought the March 14 paper to our archive room on Tuesday. We checked the caption against the scanned image, then asked Ruth to review the identification because she was named in the event program. She recognized the banner and the schedule table in the background. Those details are why we are confident the photograph is from the reopening, not from a later terminal event.
